about: Test cases for the anchoring extension 0.2.0. The values they use are in vectors.json, written by generate_vectors.py (TEST KEYS ONLY); a case names them by JSON Pointer into vectors.json. Schema cases apply a patch to a base document (base) and validate it against a schema; an empty patch tests the base itself, so each negative case differs from a valid document by the one thing it tests. Vector cases recompute values in vectors.json. Timestamp cases run the reference check of one timestamp assertion (timestamp: a pointer, or from and patch), with the export (default full, patched by export_patch), the trust policy (patched by policy_patch), the checkpoints the verifier holds (held_checkpoints) and the chain it checks (default urn:example:chain:issuer-1); every check, the timestamp and the issuer's time are expected verified unless expected says otherwise. Checkpoint cases run the reference check of one checkpoint as the verifier obtained it (checkpoint: a name in vectors.json, from and patch, issuer_checkpoint for the one in the export, or null when the source gave none; obtained_from and source_ref), with the timestamps given; every dimension is expected verified, on the stated time, unless expected says otherwise. Pairing cases read base_report, changed by report_patch, with the documents of base_context, changed as the case says, which JSON Schema cannot do. Every document a timestamp, checkpoint or pairing case gives is valid against its schema, except a checkpoint marked schema_valid false, and the reference check must give a result for it: a case in which the check raises an exception fails, whatever it expects. Patch operations: set (value, vector: a pointer into vectors.json, or digest_of: the attachment or the export as the case builds it), remove, copy (to), insert (value or vector), move (to).
